subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw make ordinary steer-mode messages abort or pause active generation to resume with the new user input, or keep steering limited to model/tool boundaries plus explicit /stop and /queue interrupt controls?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses active-run lifecycle, partial output retention, session-state ownership, and channel delivery semantics; current main only implements boundary steering and partial active non-streaming admission.

options.title: Define soft-steer as an opt-in lifecycle
options.body: Add or refresh a soft-steer queue/control path with explicit abort-or-pause, transcript, fallback, and proof requirements before changing default behavior.

options.title: Keep boundary steering only
options.body: Document that /steer and steer mode remain model-boundary mechanisms, and direct users to /stop or /queue interrupt for active generation interruption.

options.title: Split the remaining work
options.body: Track ordinary channel admission in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48003 and keep this issue for the stronger mid-generation pause/resume product decision.

recommendation.title: Define soft-steer as an opt-in lifecycle
recommendation.body: Add or refresh a soft-steer queue/control path with explicit abort-or-pause, transcript, fallback, and proof requirements before changing default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently merged adjacent terminal-session recovery work that a soft-steer lifecycle change must preserve.
